issues.legal_issue: A separate application for condonation of delay is not indispensable when the application to set aside an ex parte decree itself explains the delay and the court considers that explanation on the evidence.
material_facts: The defendants relied on an out-of-court compromise under which they understood that the plaintiff would withdraw or get the suit dismissed, and they therefore did not attend later proceedings.
They said they learned of the ex parte decree only when execution proceedings began and included that explanation in their application to set it aside.
The trial court considered the application on its merits and received evidence about the compromise and the defendants’ lack of knowledge; the appellate court found their explanation justified.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in treating the absence of a separate application for condonation of delay as fatal. The application to set aside the decree contained the necessary explanation and could be considered on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with Section 5 of the Limitation Act, an application’s substance may supply the explanation for delay; a separate application is not required where the court has considered that explanation. Procedure is the handmaid of justice. The Court distinguished Sneh Gupta v. Devi Sarup, where the applicant knew of the decree but had not sought condonation of delay.

rule.if: application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree and separate_delay_application_absent and delay_explanation_in_application and court_considered_delay_evidence

predicates.application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree: The party applied to set aside a decree entered in its absence.
predicates.separate_delay_application_absent: The party did not file a separate application asking the court to excuse delay.
predicates.delay_explanation_in_application: The application itself explained why it was not filed earlier.
predicates.court_considered_delay_evidence: The court considered evidence bearing on the explanation for the delay.

issues.definition: When a party seeking to set aside an ex parte decree explains the delay in its application and the court considers evidence about that explanation, a separate delay application is not required.

issues.legal_issue: For an application to set aside an ex parte decree, limitation runs from the applicant’s knowledge of the decree when the applicant had no notice of the decree or proceedings, and delay may in any event be excused by a satisfactory explanation.
material_facts: The defendants did not know of the proceedings or decree because they believed, based on the compromise, that the plaintiff would discontinue the suit.
The order-sheet entries relied on to suggest their presence lacked their signatures, and the appellate court found they had not attended and did not know of the proceedings.

They learned of the decree through an execution notice and filed their application within thirty days of that knowledge; the courts had also considered evidence supporting their explanation for not applying sooner.
issues.conclusion: The application was within time when limitation was reckoned from the defendants’ knowledge of the decree. Even if limitation were reckoned from the decree’s date, the delay was satisfactorily explained.
issues.legal_principle: Article 123 of the Limitation Act provides for the limitation period for setting aside an ex parte decree and, where summons have not been served, reckons time from knowledge of the decree. The Court applied that principle to the absence of notice and the later discovery of the decree. It distinguished Sneh Gupta v. Devi Sarup, where the applicant knew of the decree, and held that the supported explanation would also justify the delay if time were counted from the decree’s date.

rule.if: application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree and no_notice_of_proceedings_or_decree and knowledge_of_decree_acquired_later and application_filed_within_applicable_period_after_knowledge

predicates.application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree: The party applied to set aside a decree entered in its absence.
predicates.no_notice_of_proceedings_or_decree: The party had no notice of the proceedings or the decree before learning of it later.
predicates.knowledge_of_decree_acquired_later: The party learned of the decree after it had been entered.
predicates.application_filed_within_applicable_peri: The party filed the application within the applicable limitation period after learning of the decree.

issues.definition: When a party applying to set aside an ex parte decree had no notice of the proceedings or decree and applies within the applicable period after later learning of it, the application is timely.
